rows.abstract: Rationale: Title insurance is a new field country. There is a need for legislation to implement this provision and to encourage insurance companies to go into this venture. There is an urgency to implement title insurance system since title fraud became a very serious problem. In order to implement a system of title insurance, there is a need to amend the Insurance Code of 1978 or PD 612 as amended, by adding the necessary provisions creating the field of title insurance.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend RA No. 7610 (Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) in this direction: (1) Declaring cases involving children below twelve (12) years old shall automatically require a hold order for those accused to prevent themfrom feeling abroad; and (2) Law enforcers and members of the Judiciary and Justice Department found guilty of violations including willfully abetting these crimes or causing or assisting in the plight of those accused shall be meted out the maximumpenalty. This bill once passed into law, will help deter those in government who would conspire to allow the pedophiles to run free from justice.

rows.abstract: "Women's Medical and Hospitalization Benefits Act." Free medical and hospitalization benefits shall be granted to indigent Filipino women suffering from women's diseases, such as cancer of the reproductive organ, cancer of the breast and pregnancy-relat ed diseases; illnesses and injuries due to violence inflicted on women. For this purpose, a special ward shall be established in all provincial and district hospitals.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to institute a children's fund which shall be managed by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) for the protection and rehabilitation of abandoned, abused and sexually exploited children. By giving these children theproper environment they need, they can fully realize their own potentials and actively participate in community life and nation-building .

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PROTECTION AGAINST COMPUTER FRAUD, ABUSES AND OTHER CYBER-RELATED FRAUDULENT ACTIVITIES, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Computer Fraud and Abuses Act of 2001." The need for a special legislation against computer crimes is the primary objective of this proposed measure. This bill defines computer fraud and the offenses covered by the term "computer forgery, damage to computer data or computer programs, computer sabotage, unauthorized access and unauthorized interception as well as obscenities. It likewise, provides the necessary penal provisions that must be imposed upon the violators of the offense, both fine and imprisonment. Finally, it accords authority to the National Security Council to conduct investigation on computer-relate d crimes vis-a-vis its effects on national security.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The State shall undertake a continuing program of urban land reform and housing which will make available at affordable costs decent housing and basic services to underprivileged and homeless citizens. Towards this end, the government shall, in cooperation with the private sector, actively pursue the provision of housing to the people as a means of attaining a socially just society. The government shall regard housing not as a mere provision of shelter but as a cyclic process by which economic activity may dynamically be induced.> The government shall likewise pursue an urban development that directly responds to the welfare, health, and safety of the public.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Private individuals and/or entities, by way of a legitimate deed, conditionally donates, or in any other manner conditionally transfer, in gratuity, its ownership and physical possession of a certain property to the government, any of itsinstrumentality , or government-owne d or-controlled corporation. The deed of conveyance provides that the donee shall introduce improvements, infrastructure or otherwise, to the property, however, with the condition tht should the donee violates any of the term and/or conditions of the transfer, the ownership and possession of the property automatically reverts bacj to the donor, including all the improvements introduced thereto by the donee, which in this case the government. > At face value,, this arrangement is perfectly legal and tenable. However, the question of propriety arises when, after the government introduces improvements in the property, the donor influences the concerned government official or employee of the government char

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to create the Department of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (DFAR) to ensure the preservation and enhance the proper development of the Philippine water and marine resources. The proposed Department shall manage, develop, protect, conserve and utilize all fisheries and aquatic resources of the country except for municipal waters, which shall remain under the jurisdiction, capture, processing and marketing of fisheries and marine products, as well as streamline all the agencies presently involved, or has something to do, in the fishery sector.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PRODUCTION OF FILMS THAT DEPICT THE LIFE STORIES OF CRIMINALS FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to uphold the rule of law and demand compliance therewith by enforcing penalties. The State shall prohibit the production of films depicting the life stories of criminals, thereby depriving them of the opportunity to profit from their misdeeds by selling the film rights of their life stories. The State shall likewise, penalize unscrupulous film producers who glorify criminals by producing films that draw bias towards the criminal and in the process depriving the movie goind public the right to an intelligent, decent, respectable and wholesome entertainment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2001-07-30

rows.abstract: Any incumbent public officer against whom any criminal prosecution under a valid information under this Act or under Title 7, Book II of the Revised Penal Code or for any offense involving fraud upon government or public funds or property whether asa simple or as a complex offense and in whatever stage of execution and mode of participation, is pending in court, shall be suspended from office, EXCEPT WHEN HE IS ALREADY OCCUPYING AN OFFICE WHICH IS NOT TASKED WITH THE CUSTODY OF DOCUMENTS THATMAY BE USED AGAINST HIM NOR EXERCISES DIRECT OR INDIRECT ADMINISTRATIVE SUPERVISION OVER SUCH PERSONS SO TASKED OR OTHER WITNESS FOR THE PROSECUTION. > THE PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION SHALL BE FOR A PERIOD OF NOT EXCEEDING NINETY (90) DAYS. IT SHALL BE IMPPOSED ONLY AFTER ARRAIGNMENT: PROVIDED, THAT SHOULD THE PROSECUTION'S PRESENTATION OF EVIDENCE BE TERMINATED PRIOR TO THE LAPSE OF THE PREVENTIVE SUSPENSION PERIOD, THE SUSPENSION SHALL AUTOMATICALLY BE LIFTED.

rows.title_full: AN ACT RATIONALIZING THE HOUSING SECTOR CREATING THEREBY THE DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, DEFINING ITS STRUCTURE, PROVIDING FOR ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Shelter is a basic need and fundamental right of the Filipino people. As such, the State is duty-bound to implement to implement a housing program that is affordable, adequate and decent. Despite the presence of government institutions that ensure the financing of housing units, there is still a pressing need to rationalize the housing sector to be able to reach out to the broadest units, there is still a pressing need to rationalize the housing sector to be able to reach out to the broadest number of people, especially the more needy and marginalized ones.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04517

rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE CHAIN DISTRIBUTION PLANS OR PYRAMID SALES SCHEMES AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-THREE HUNDRED AND NINETY-FOUR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Pyramiding companies are merely sales structures devised to recruit people who want to make fast money, where the value of the product or the customer base is questionable. They usually offer products with no real value and operate on the principleof making payments for recruiting others. When the inevitable saturation occurs, the people at the bottom in the pyramid run out of prospects to join the organization and lose money. Unless and until the operation of these "chain distribution plans or pyramid sales schemes" are completely banned, their activities will continue to undermine the operation of legitimate multi-level marketing companies and, by and large, affect the country's economy.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05601

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGTHENING VOLUNTARY ARBITRATION AS A PREFERENTIAL MODE OF LABOR DISPUTE SETTLEMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLES 260, 261, 262-A, 262-B AND 277 (F) OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend five (5) articles of PD 442 (Labor Code) on matters, such as the following: (1) the selection of the voluntary arbitrators or a panel of Voluntary Arbitrators; (2) the redefining jurisdiction of the body to hear cases of termination of workers, productivity schemes or wage distortions arising from legislated or mandated wage increases; (3) meting out providing sanctions against erring arbitrators; (4) determining the fees of the arbitrators; and (5) providing subsidy for unions that cannot shoulder the fees of the arbitrators.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE BENEFITS OF RETIRED GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMONWEALTH ACT NUMBERED ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY-SIX, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Under this bill, government employees who retire under either  RA 660 or PD 1146 would be receiving six (6) year-annual lump sum instead of the usual five (5) year annually. Further, the basis of the monthly annuity to be subsequently received is proposed to be the highest monthly salary rate received prior to retirement in lieu of the existing provision which provides that the basis of the annuity is the average monthly salary received during the last three years of service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING GOVERNMENT OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES FROM PLAYING IN CASINOS AND OTHER SIMILAR ESTABLISHMENTS OPERATED  BY THE PHILIPPINE AMUSEMENT AND GAMING CORPORATION, OR BY OTHER SIMILAR GOVERNMENT-OWNE D OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS, AND THEIRFRANCHISE HOLDERS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: All elective and appointive government officers and employees, regardless of rank, designation, and status of employment, are hereby prohibited from playing in casinos amd other similar establishments operated by the Philippine Amusement and GamingCorporation. Such ban shall include entry inside casino premises during the establishment's business hours.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO STRENGTHEN LOCAL ENVIRONMENT PROTECTION BY MAKING THE APPOINTMENT OF AN ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES OFFICER MANDATORY FOR PROVINCIAL, CITY AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 484 (A) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160,OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991'
rows.abstract: The fragiles situation of our ecology alone should have prodded past policymakers to make its protection the number one priority of government. But in the so-called Magna Carta of local governments, the designation of the officer responsible or thecare of the environment was not given paramount importance. In case of oversight, if not insensitivity, the naming of an environment and natural resources officer was reduced into an option. This bill attempts to correct this oversight by making it mandatory for city, provincial and municipal governments to appoint an environment and natural officer was reduced into an option. > This bill attempts to correct this oversight by making it mandatory for city, provincial and municipal government to aappoint an environmental and natural resources officer.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR THE KILLING, WOUNDING OR TAKING AWAY OF THE EAGLE AND/OR DESTROYING, DISTURBING OR TAKING AWAY OF THE BIRD'S NESTS OR EGGS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION FIVE OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY-SEVEN
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Philippine Eagle is a symbol of all life in the rain forest. Just as this bird depends on the rain forests to survive, the earth's survival likewise lies on the preservation of the forests. If the eagle disappears, it means the support forest has disappeared. The survival of the eagle means the survival of our race.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MINIMUM SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS IN ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS FROM SALARY GRADE 10 TO SALARY GRADE 18 AND AUTHORIZING THE APPROPRIATION OF FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The present minimum salary grade level of public schoolteachers in the elementary and secondary school levels, regardless of their employment status, shall be upgraded to Salary Grade 18 per month: Provided, That the salary upgrading shall be differentiated in accordance with qualifications, skills, length of service and other logical bases of differentiation : Provided, further, That merit promotion on the basis of performance evaluation results shall be considered and treated as separate anddistinct from the upgraded salary provided for under this Act: Provided, further, That the salary upgrading shall not result to salary distortions, as defined under existing laws, within the Department of Education, Culture and Sports.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE ALLOWANCES/HONO RARIA OF AND GRANTING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991'
rows.abstract: In recognition of the invaluable service rendered by barangay officials, this bill seeks to increase the minimum monthly allowances/hono raria from One Thousand Pesos (P1,000.00) to Six Thousand Pesos (P6,000.00) for barangay captains and from Six Hundred Pesos (P600) to Three Thousand Pesos (P3,000.00) for the sangguniang barangay members, barangay secretaries, and barangay treasurers. It also grants retirement benefits to all barangay officials who have served at least nine (9) years of cumulative service a lump sum retirement benefit equivalent to seventy-five percent (75%) of their monthly allowance/honor arium per year of service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETAIL OR ASSIGNMENT OF MILITARY PERSONNEL IN CIVILIAN OFFICES AND PUBLIC UTILITIES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: No military personnel shall be assigned or detailed to take over the functions of any civilian post in any civilian office or agency of the government as well as in public utilities and in government-owne d and-controlled corporations except in times of war or other national emergency. Service of military personnel in civilian offices or agencies of the government and in government-owne d or-controlled corporations and/or their subsidiaries, as well as in public utilities are hereby terminated.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE since 2001-07-30

Earnings of each depository account shall accrue exclusively thereto.

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING MEDICAL NEUTRALITY BY REPEALING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 169, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 212, WHICH REQUIRES ANY ATTENDING PHYSICIAN OF ANY HOSPITAL, MEDICAL CLINIC, SANITARIUM OR OTHER MEDICAL ESTABLISHMENTS OR ANY MEDICAL PRACTITIONER WHO HAS TREATED ANY PERSON FOR SERIOUS OR LESS SERIOUS PHYSICAL INJURIES TO REPORT THE FACT OF TREATMENT
rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to repeal the decree which requires physicians and medical practitioners to report their treatment of any person for physical injuries to the nearest government health authority. By compelling physicians to make such notifications, Presidential Decree No. 169, later amended by the Aquino-era Executive Order No. 212, clearly treats at the time-honored patient-doctor confidentiality of relationship. The physician's oath commands him to treat any person in distress regardless of the latter's creed, color, religion or nationality. That the patient's well-being and recovery, in the order of prioties precede none. If compliance to PD 169 would jeopardize his patient's life, then a physician has all the rights to rage aagainst such intrusion.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-30

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to bring back the Filipinos' trust on the banking industry as it proposed to increase the maximum amount of insured deposits from the current P100,000.00 to P500,000.00 and establish a deposit insurance coverage plan for deposits inexcess of P500,000.00 which a depositor may have an option to enroll in at his/her cost. Accordingly, the bill increases the permanent insurance fund from the current amount of P3 billion to P8 billion.

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING FROM INCOME TAXATION CERTAIN RENTALS ON RESIDENTIAL/APA RTMENT OR OTHER DWELLING UNITS, ALLOWING THEM TO BE DEDUCTIBLE FROM TAXATION FIXED INCOME OF THE TENANTS OR INDIVIDUALS WHO PAY SAID RENTALS
rows.abstract: Rentals or leases paid during a taxable period by tenants or individuals for occupancy of residential/apa rtment or dwelling units shall be exempted from internal revenue tax and shall be deductible from their taxable fixed income earned during thesaid taxable period: Provided, that the amount of rentals or leases covered by such exemption shall not exceed Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) per month for those residing within Metro Manila, Two Thousand Five Hundred Pesos (P2,500.00) per month forthose residing outside of Matro Manila: and Provided, further that such payments are duly covered by valid rental or lease contract agreement/s for occupancy of the residential/apa rtment or dwelling unit/s and by official receipts indicating paymennt of rentals/leases for purposes of establishing authenticity of claims for tax exemptions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL IRRIGATED AND IRRIGABLE AGRICULTURAL LANDS AS PROTECTED AREAS FOR AGRICULTURE, PROHIBITING ITS CONVERSION FOR USES OTHER THAN AGRICULTURAL, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 20 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: "National Protected Areas for Agriculture (NPAA) Law." Main thrusts of this proposal are: (1) Grant of direct access to the latest agricultural technology, electric power, water sources, roads, credit and domestic markets to agricultural areas; (2)Essential research support for the intensive and environmentally -friendly development of food production; and (3) Prioritized allotment of the country's best alluvial soils for intensive agricultural activity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE, FOOD & FISHERIES since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDEFINING THE CRIME OF PLUNDER THEREBY AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY HUNDRED AND EIGTHY, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-SIX HUNDRED AND FIFTY-NINE
rows.abstract: This bill redefines the crime of plunder by further lowering the aggregate amount involved to P25,000,000.00. Indeed, the present level of P50,000,000.00 is seemingly ineffective. It has not deterred public officials from committeing various forms of corruption as exposes after exposes hug newspaper headlines.

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT SECURITY, INTELLIGENCE AND CONFIDENTIAL FUNDS BE SUBJECTED TO STANDARD AUDITING PROCEDURES, REQUIRING THE SUBMISSION OF THE AUDIT AND LIQUIDATION REPORTS ON SAID FUNDS TO THE HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FORVIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: The confidential audit of these funds, in the guise of protecting the source of "bought" information, has spawned a culture of corruption in the intelligence community. By perpetuating the myth that national security operations are off-limits to civilians, a thich veil of secrecy has blanketed what has become a defacto republic within our armed forces. > This bill does not intend to pry open the operations of our intelligence community. Logic and the safety of our soldiers dictate that some businesses are better conducted in the dark. But the accounting of taxpayers' money should be  made under the sun. More so, if such money currently runs into billions of pesos a year.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-30

rows.abstract: SECTION 1. A new section, to be numbered Two Hundred Eight-Seven, shall be added to Chapter 2, Title XI of the National Internal Revenue Code, to read as follows: "SEC. 287. DISPOSITION OF PROCEEDS OF VALUE-ADDED TAX.  (A) IN GENERAL. - FIFTY PERCENT (50%) OF THE VALUE-ADDED TAX COLLECTED UNDER TITLE IV OF THIS CODE SHALL BE ALLOCATED TO EXPENDITURES FOR HEALTH AND EDUCATION SERVICES, IRRIGATION AND POST-HARVEST FACILITIES, HOUSING, ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION, AND TRAINING AND CAPABILITY BUILDINGPROGRAMS FOR MICRO-FINANCES, FOR A PERIOD OF FIVE YEARS IN THE FOLLOWING PROPORTIONS: EDUCATION 25%;  HEALTH 25%; AGRICULTURAL FACILITIES AND SERVICES  25%; HOUSING  15%; ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION 5%:;  TRAINING AND CAPABILITY BUILDING PROGRAMS 5%.

rows.author: C091
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09287) enacted on 2004-04-02
rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING HIGHER AND SIMULTANEOUS PENALTIES OF PRISON TERM AND FINE FOR VIOLATIONS OF GAMBLING LAWS WHENEVER THE OFFENDER IS THE MAINTAINER, CONDUCTOR, BANKER OR GAMBLING LORD, AND ADDITIONAL PENALTY IF THE OFFENDER IS A POLICE OR MILITARYOFFICER OR PERSONNEL OR A LOCAL GOVERNMENT OFFICIAL, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 1 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1602

rows.status: Substituted by HB06575

rows.author: C091
rows.title_full: AN ACT BANNING THE ENTRY, SALE, PROCESSING, FIELD TESTING AND RELEASE OF PRODUCTS CONSISTING OF, CONTAINING OR DERIVED FROM GENETICALLY MODIFIED ORGANISMS (GMOs) INTO AND WITHIN THE COUNTRY AND IMPOSING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: "GMO Prohibition Act of 2000." Rationale: We are not a nation of guinea pigs. But the entry into the country of genetically engineered crops and food products with genetically modified organisms (GMOs) may just as well make us one. We have yet to determine the risks and hazards of biotechnology to health and the environment and until then it is incumbent upon government to impose measures that would safeguard our people's interests and welfare.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-30

rows.author: C065
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A LIVING WAGE TO EMPLOYEES AND WORKERS IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTORS, ESTABLISHING THE MECHANISM AND PROPER STANDARDS THEREFOR, REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 6727, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Living Wage Act of 2001." Among the salient features of this bill are: (1) Full-time employees and workers in the public and private agricultural and nonagricultural sectors shall receive a living wage equivalent to the cost of living for a familyof six (6); (2) Congress shall set the minimum standards for "basket of goods" in determining the cost of living equivalent of the living wage;  (3) Congress shall initially determine the living wage rates which shall thereafter be set by the LivingWage Commission proposed to be created under the bill, etc.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A DRUG REHABILITATION CENTER IN EVERY REGION OF THE COUNTRY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: It is by the establishment of a rehabilitation center in every region of the country that we can make accessible to every drug dependent medical facilities for a speedy recovery from the physical and mental trauma brought about by dangerous drugs. Hence, approval of this bill is earnestly recommended.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2001-07-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF FISHERIES AND OCEANS, PROVIDING FOR THE TRANSFER OF POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE ON FISHERY MATTERS TO SAID DEPARTMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: According to the National Statistics Office, the population of the Philippines is estimated to reach 77.925 million by the year 2001. The total projected domestic requirements for fish will be 3 million metric tons to adequately feed ourpeople.  The Philippines only ranks number 13 in world catch of fish, crustaceans and mulls behind our Asian neighbors and other countries. Tailand, Korea, and Taiwan have already surpassed us in fish production and technology. Mr. Edgardo G. Sarrosa, Chairman of the Chamber of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources complains that there is now some 18 major agencies of the government dealing on fishery matters but there is no consolidated efforts to project fisheries as a food source considering that iit contributes some 82 billion pesos yearly to the Philippine economy. Hence there is an imperative need for a strong and separate Department of Fisheries and Oceans so that the Philippines will be at par with our Asian neighbors.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A SPECIAL TASK FORCE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE TO APPREHEND PERSONS WITH PENDING WARRANTS OF ARREST AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: For the effective and expeditious dispensation of justice, a special task force should be created and charged with the obligatory task to serve the warrants of arrest and detain the persons thus arrested.  As envisioned, this special taskforce is composed of selected personnel on detail from the different agencies of the government and under the direct supervision of the SEcretary of Justice. This task force will have enough resources and more competent personnel to track down and effect services of warrants of arrest to the persons concerned.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING VACATION LEAVE BENEFITS OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Any provision of existing law to the contrary notwithstanding , an employee, whether permanent or temporary, of the National Government, its branches, agencies and instrumentality 's, including local governments, and of government-owne d and or controlled corporations and their subsidiaries, shall be entitled to thirty days annual vacation leave with full pay, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Holiday, for each calendar year of service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF THE INDETERMINATE SENTENCE LAW, AS AMENDED, BY PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY PAROLE OF PRISONERS WHO SHALL HAVE SERVED AT LEAST TEN(10) YEARS OF HIS/HER SENTENCE WITH GOOD BEHAVIOR
rows.abstract: Rationale:  It is a fact that penal institutions throughout the country are over-congested because of the rapid increase in criminally and confinement of criminals in detention and prison cells. To decongest our already congested detention and prison cells, there are two alternatives that should be done by the government, namely:  (1) build, upgrade and expand more existing ones and (2) deconggest the penal institutions by accelerating the parole program.  The first alternative will be very expensive but certainly, the second alternative will be very much economical.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR TRANSPARENCY IN THE BUDGET PROCESS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION THIRTY-ONE OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED ONE THOUSAND ONE HUNDRED SEVENTY-SEVEN, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE BUDGET REFORM DECREE, AS CODIFIED UNDER SECTION TWENTY-SIX, BOOK VI OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NUMBERED TWO-HUNDRED NINETY-TWO, ALSO KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987; AND REPEALING PROVISIONS OF LAWS AUTHORIZING AUTOMATIC APPROPRIATIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Section thirty-one Presidential Decree No. 1177 as codified in Section twenty-six, Book VI, of Executive Order Numbered two hundred ninety-two, is hereby amended to read as follows: "Sec. 31 [Automatic] Appropriations. - All expenditures for (a) personal retirement premiums, government service insurance and other similar fixed expenditures, (b) principal and interest on public debt (c) national government guarantees of obligations which are drawn upon [are automatically appropriated] SHALL BE SUBJECT TO THE REGULAR ANNUAL CONGRESSIONAL APPROPRIATIONS: Provided, That no obligation shall be incurred or interest made from funds thus [automatically] appropriated except, as issued in the form of regular budgetary allotments."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE `GALING PINOY' AWARD PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: The condition of the Filipino entrepreneurs and the workers to the development of the country's economy must be recognized and rewarded. There is a need to focus national attention to their invaluable contributions to the economy and thecountry as a whole and provide attractive incentives to bolster their competitiveness .  They deserve motivation and recognition which can take the form of giving them honors, privileges, and cash awards.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROMOTION OF A CITY OR MUNICIPAL TRIAL COURT JUDGE TO THE POSITION OF A REGIONAL TRIAL COURT JUDGE UPON RETIREMENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill takes note of the plight of city and municipal judge by providing that they shall be promoted to the rank of a Regional Trial Court judges upon their retirement. Thus, with their upgrading pension, they will be able to live a life with dignity after devoting the fruitful years of their lives to the dispensation of justice.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ORGANIZATION OF COOPERATIVES FOR FRY GATHERERS, SMALL SCALE FISHERMEN AND SMALL FISHFARMERS
rows.abstract: "Fry gatherers" refers to an individual, usually self-employed, who is engaged in the catching, gathering or collecting of fish fry with the use of nets, traps, or other fishing gears for the purpose of selling them. "Organization of Cooperatives" refers to fry gatherers, small-scale fishermen and small fishfarmers shall be organized as cooperatives and be registered under Republic Act Numbered Six Thousand Nine-hundred Thirty-nine under the supervision of the Cooperative Development Authority.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A NEW PERIOD OF REGISTRATION OF COUNTRYSIDE AND BARANGAY BUSINESS ENTERPRISES (CBBE) UNDER THE KALAKALAN TWENTY PROGRAM FROM DECEMBER 1, 1998 TO NOVEMBER 30, 2008
rows.abstract: Subject to the rules and regulations formulated to implement the provisions of Republic Act No. 6810, there shall be a new period of registration of Countryside and Barangay Business Enterprises (CBBE) from December 1, 1998 to November 30, 2008.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 26 (2) OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIX THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED SEVENTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `THE OMBUDSMAN ACT OF 1989', IN RELATION TO SECTION 12 OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE THOUSAND NINETEEN, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed amendment to RA No. 6770 reads as follows: "The Office of the Ombudsman shall receive complaints from (any source in whatever form) ANY PERSON DULY IDENTIFIED AS AN ACCUSER WHICH MUST BE VERIFIED AND UNDER OATH concerning an official act or omission. It shall act on the complaint immediately provided that the complaint is substantially true and well-founded and if it finds the same entirely baseless, it shall dismiss the same and inform the complainant of such dismissal citing thereasons therefore.  If it finds a reasonable ground to investigate further, it shall first furnish the respondent public officer or employee with a summary of the complaint and require him to submit a written answer within seventy-two hours from receeipt thereof: PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT DURING THE PENDENCY OF THE CASE, THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN OR ANY PRINT-MEDIA FOR THAT MATTER SHALL NOT PUBLISH THE CASE COVERED BY THE COMPLAINT.  If the answer is found satisfactory, it shall dismiss the case
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-31

rows.title_full: AN ACT SHORTENING THE PERIOD TO CARRY OUT THE EXECUTION OF THE CONVICT, FROM ONE (1) YEAR TO SIX (6) MONTHS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION TWENTY-FOUR OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-SIX FIFTY-NINE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale:  On December 13, 1993, Republic Act No. 7659 was enacted into law re-imposing the death penalty, this time by lethal injection instead of the much ballyhooed electrocution. The agony of waiting should be shortened to give the society theneeded psychological and moral peace. For it cannot be denied that while the crime perpetrator are given their due, the victims suffer a lifetime trauma, together with their families and loved ones, which trauma can not be easily forgotten, no one (1) year period is too long as a waiting period.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-31
